sprint.goal: Add JWT-based user authentication: login, register, protect task endpoints

sprint_history.goal: Build a lightweight Kanban project management app: REST API + minimal web UI. Users can create tasks, move them between Todo, In Progress, and Done, edit task details, and delete tasks.

tasks.title: Create tasks table schema (id, title, status, created_at) in database.py
Implement REST API in server.py: create/list/update/delete tasks, move between statuses
Build Kanban board UI in index.html (3 columns, click-to-move) consuming the API

messages.content: database.py now exposes initialize_database(), get_connection(), utc_timestamp(), DATABASE_PATH, and VALID_STATUSES; tasks uses id, title, status, created_at with valid statuses todo/in_progress/done.

API ready: GET/POST /api/tasks; PATCH or PUT /api/tasks/:id; DELETE /api/tasks/:id. Tasks return id, title, status (todo|in_progress|done), created_at. POST requires title and accepts optional status; PATCH accepts title and/or status.
Frontend is complete and consumes the implemented task API; the board supports Todo, In Progress, and Done workflows.

QA found a minor UX gap: edit-form submission closes the dialog even when the PATCH request fails because mutate() catches errors internally. Keeping it open on failed saves would let users retry immediately.

Security review passed: API limits JSON request bodies, validates task fields/statuses, uses SQLite parameters for values, escapes frontend task text via textContent, and constrains static files to the static directory.

sprint_history.retrospective: Sprint retrospective: Architecture established the stdlib contract; database delivered the constrained schema; backend implemented validated CRUD; frontend integrated the three-column board; QA added and passed lifecycle coverage while noting the failed-save dialog UX gap; security verified input, SQL, rendering, and static-path safeguards; manager coordinated the completed handoffs.

sprint_history.goal: Add JWT-based user authentication: login, register, protect task endpoints

tasks.title: Define the standard-library authentication design: user model, password hashing, signed JWT claims/expiry, API contract, and task ownership rules.
Add a users schema and migrate task ownership in database.py, including unique usernames and secure password-hash storage fields.
Implement register/login endpoints, standard-library JWT signing and verification, and Bearer-token protection plus per-user scoping for task endpoints in server.py.
Add register/login UI and authenticated task requests in static/index.html, retaining a token only for the browser session and handling unauthenticated responses.
Add regression coverage for registration, login, token expiry/invalid-token rejection, protected task endpoints, and task isolation between users.
Review password hashing, JWT signing/verification, token handling, authorization boundaries, and auth error responses after implementation.

messages.content: Use users(id, username UNIQUE, password_hash, password_salt, created_at) and associate every task with user_id; do not expose unowned legacy tasks.
Use PBKDF2-HMAC with random salts; issue HS256 JWTs with sub, iat, exp; require Authorization: Bearer tokens and scope all task access by sub.
Keep the returned token in sessionStorage, attach it to task requests, and show the signed-out state after a 401.

Database auth schema is ready: users has id, case-insensitive unique username, password_hash BLOB, password_salt BLOB, created_at; tasks now has nullable user_id referencing users(id). Connections enable foreign keys, and unowned legacy tasks remain inaccessible when queries scope by user_id.

Auth API ready: POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/login require exactly {username,password}; both return {token,user}. Usernames are 3–64 chars using letters/numbers/._-, passwords are 8–256 chars. Send Authorization: Bearer <token> for every /api/tasks request; 401 means show signed-out UI.

Set KANBAN_JWT_SECRET to at least 32 bytes in test setup. Auth coverage can use POST /api/auth/register/login; unauthenticated task routes return 401, and a second user receives 404 when mutating another user's task.

Server uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 16-byte random salts and 310,000 iterations; JWTs are HS256, require sub/iat/exp, use constant-time signature comparison, expire after one hour, and require KANBAN_JWT_SECRET (minimum 32 bytes).

tasks.title: Audit and confirm the standard-library JWT authentication contract, including token claims, password hashing, error responses, and task ownership boundaries.
Verify and complete the users/task-ownership schema migration in database.py for authentication and per-user task isolation.
Verify and complete register/login, HS256 JWT verification, Bearer protection, and per-user task authorization in server.py.
Complete the login/register UI and session-scoped Bearer-token integration in static/index.html.
Test registration, login, invalid and expired token handling, protected task routes, and cross-user task isolation.
Review the completed authentication implementation for password storage, JWT validation, token handling, and authorization bypasses.

messages.content: Schema contract is confirmed: retain case-insensitive unique users and nullable migrated tasks.user_id; authenticated queries must always filter by the JWT user id.
API contract is confirmed: public POST /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login return {token,user}; all task routes require Bearer HS256 tokens with valid sub, iat, and exp claims.
Complete the pending auth UI against the confirmed contract: sessionStorage token only, Authorization Bearer header on task requests, and signed-out handling for 401 responses.

Database verification passed: legacy tasks migrate with NULL user_id, usernames are case-insensitively unique, and foreign keys reject unknown task owners. Continue filtering every authenticated task operation by user_id.
Backend contract remains ready: register/login return {token,user}; task endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token>; a 401 response should clear the session and show authentication controls.

Backend auth checks passed for registration, protected task creation, anonymous 401 rejection, and cross-user 404 rejection. Update legacy task tests to authenticate and set KANBAN_JWT_SECRET in test setup.

Frontend auth integration is complete: users can register/login, the JWT is kept only in sessionStorage, task requests carry a Bearer token, sign-out clears it, and 401 responses return users to the sign-in UI.

Sprint 3 QA passed: 4 regression tests cover registration/login, stored password derivation, protected CRUD, cross-user isolation, tampered and expired token rejection, plus the frontend authentication integration markers.

Security follow-up: _login returns immediately when a username is absent but runs PBKDF2 for existing users, creating a measurable username-enumeration timing difference if the server is exposed. Run PBKDF2 against a fixed dummy salt/hash before returning the same 401 response for unknown users.

Security sign-off is pending a small login timing-enumeration mitigation. All other reviewed controls are present: random salts with PBKDF2, required environment secret, strict HS256 validation with constant-time HMAC comparison, sessionStorage-only frontend token handling, and user-scoped task mutations.

architecture_decisions.decision: Python stdlib http.server + sqlite3 for backend, single static HTML+vanilla JS file for frontend. No external dependencies (sandbox has no network access).
Used a SQLite CHECK constraint to restrict task statuses to todo, in_progress, and done.
Used JSON request/response bodies and PATCH for partial task edits/status moves.
Validated titles and status values at the API boundary; used parameterized SQLite statements.
Kept the UI as a single static HTML file using vanilla JavaScript and CSS.
Used a status selector on every card to provide direct click-based movement between board columns.
Used an in-process handler harness so API tests exercise the real handler and SQLite logic without opening a network socket.
Verified Python compilation, frontend JavaScript syntax, and whitespace checks in addition to the lifecycle test.

The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, which is appropriate for this unauthenticated local Kanban app; it should not be deployed on a public interface without adding authentication and authorization.
Retain the existing 16 KiB request-body limit and resolved-path containment check for static files.
Use Python standard-library hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with a random per-user salt for password storage; never store plaintext passwords.
Implement compact JWTs with base64url JSON, HS256 HMAC signatures, and constant-time signature comparison. Require sub, iat, and exp claims; reject malformed, expired, or wrong-algorithm tokens.
Load the JWT signing secret from an environment variable at server startup and do not hard-code it or return it in API responses.
Register/login are public POST routes; every task route requires a Bearer token and uses its subject to enforce task ownership.
Keep the frontend as one static HTML file and hold the access token in sessionStorage rather than persistent localStorage.
Passwords use salted PBKDF2-HMAC; plaintext passwords are never persisted.
JWTs use base64url-encoded HS256 signatures with constant-time comparison and required sub, iat, and exp claims.
The signing secret is supplied through the server environment and is never hard-coded or returned.
Only registration and login remain public; task routes are authenticated and user-scoped.
Kept task.user_id nullable for migration compatibility; authenticated task queries must always filter user_id to prevent access to legacy unowned rows.
Used BLOB columns for derived password hashes and salts, a case-insensitive unique username constraint, and an index on tasks.user_id.
The server refuses to start without a KANBAN_JWT_SECRET of at least 32 bytes.
Task update and deletion intentionally return 404 for another user's task to avoid exposing task existence.
Keep Python stdlib only: PBKDF2-HMAC with per-user random salts for passwords and HMAC-SHA256 for compact JWT signing.
Require KANBAN_JWT_SECRET at startup, validate HS256 exactly, compare signatures in constant time, and reject malformed or expired tokens.
Keep task ownership server-enforced in every SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE; unauthenticated access returns 401 and cross-user mutations return 404.
No database changes were needed; the existing migration meets the confirmed authentication and ownership contract.
No backend changes were needed after verification: HS256 JWT validation, password hashing, Bearer parsing, startup-secret enforcement, and per-user task filters satisfy the confirmed contract.
Stored only the JWT in sessionStorage; user display details remain in page memory rather than persistent browser storage.
Kept the edit dialog open if a task-save request fails, addressing the prior QA UX observation.
Tests use an in-process handler harness and temporary SQLite database, avoiding network sockets while exercising the real request handlers and schema.
The test fixture supplies KANBAN_JWT_SECRET explicitly so authentication tests do not rely on a developer-machine secret.
Do not expose this unauthenticated-by-default server beyond localhost until login timing is equalized and additional abuse controls are considered.
Continue rejecting malformed/expired tokens and returning 404 for cross-user task mutations to avoid resource-existence disclosure.
